Blood counts check red cells that carry oxygen, white cells that help fight infection and platelets that help stop bleeding. Low counts can lead to a pause, a lower prescribed dose, a transfusion or further tests. Persistent or unexplained changes sometimes need specialist bone-marrow tests to investigate myelodysplastic syndrome or acute myeloid leukaemia (MDS/AML). These are serious conditions; their risk differs by treatment setting and previous therapy. A treatment pause is not itself a diagnosis. There is no universal routine white-cell growth-factor course.

Give the pharmacist a complete list of prescriptions, over-the-counter medicines, vitamins and herbal products. Some antibiotics, antifungals, seizure medicines and St John’s wort can change how much olaparib reaches your body. Even anti-sickness treatment needs checking: aprepitant can increase olaparib exposure. Do not start a borrowed support medicine, change the olaparib dose or restart a paused course yourself.
NCCP allows consideration of a proton pump inhibitor under local policy. This is symptom- and patient-dependent, rather than a compulsory medication for everyone.
Only the treating team can confirm when and at what dose to restart. Do not take catch-up doses after a pause.

If you could become pregnant, use two reliable complementary contraception methods during treatment and for six months after the last dose, following your team’s advice. A partner who could become pregnant should also use highly effective contraception. Do not donate sperm during treatment or for three months afterwards; discuss fertility preservation before treatment if relevant.

Olaparib toxicity ladder: 300 → 250 → 200 mg twice daily. Grade 4 febrile neutropenia can prompt consideration of a two-level reduction after recovery. Do not issue a restart dose during an unresolved hold or invent a third toxicity level below 200 mg twice daily.

Severe cytopenia or transfusion dependence: interrupt olaparib and investigate. Persistent clinically abnormal counts after a 4-week interruption require haematology/marrow and cytogenetic investigation. Suspected MDS/AML requires investigation; only confirmed MDS/AML requires permanent olaparib discontinuation.

Suspected pneumonitis: interrupt olaparib and investigate; confirmed pneumonitis: discontinue olaparib. Suspected DILI: interrupt and investigate; severe DILI can require discontinuation. Neither pathway is replaced by a reassuring chronic hepatic class.

Concordant CrCl above 30 through 50 mL/min supports 200 mg twice daily, subject to other restrictions; above 50 does not automatically re-escalate an already reduced dose. Exactly 30, below 30/dialysis and Child–Pugh C require source reconciliation.

If a strong CYP3A inhibitor is unavoidable, the source-specific olaparib dose is 100 mg twice daily; for a moderate inhibitor it is 150 mg twice daily after review. These are interaction doses, not steps in the toxicity ladder.

Swallow the prescribed tablets whole with or without food, once in the morning and once in the evening. Do not chew, crush, dissolve or divide them. If you miss a dose, take the next normal dose at its usual time; do not double up. Do not substitute olaparib capsules for tablets. Avoid grapefruit juice and check other grapefruit or bitter-orange products with your pharmacist.

BRCA1 and BRCA2 help repair damaged DNA. A germline change is present in the body’s cells and may have implications for relatives. A tumour-only change does not by itself show that it is inherited. evidence_at_a_glance.qualitative_result: OlympiA compared one year of olaparib with placebo after chemotherapy and local treatment in 1,836 people with germline BRCA1/2-associated, high-risk HER2-negative early breast cancer. At six years, estimated invasive disease-free survival was 79.6% with olaparib and 70.3% with placebo; estimated overall survival was 87.5% and 83.2%. Invasive disease-free survival counts specified invasive-cancer events or death, not just breast recurrence. These descriptive follow-up results support benefit after the planned one-year course; they do not mean six years of tablets or predict your personal outcome.

evidence_at_a_glance.qualitative_result: SOLO1 compared olaparib with placebo in 391 people with newly diagnosed advanced BRCA-mutated ovarian, fallopian-tube or primary-peritoneal cancer responding to platinum. The main published 2018 endpoint was time without progression or death. In the original analysis, the estimated proportion alive without cancer progression at three years was 60% with olaparib and 27% with placebo. This supports maintenance treatment after a response. The figure is a trial-group estimate, not an individual forecast or a three-year tablet course.
limitations: The study population was specifically selected for BRCA-mutated first-line disease. Results are not a direct comparison with olaparib plus bevacizumab and should not be transferred to relapsed disease.

urgent_review_signals: Call your oncology team urgently for fever, shaking chills, feeling suddenly unwell, unusual bruising or bleeding, marked weakness, new or worsening cough or breathlessness, a new painful swollen limb, yellow skin or eyes, dark urine, persistent vomiting or diarrhoea, or inability to keep fluids down. Follow your own temperature and contact plan; do not wait for the next appointment. Severe breathing difficulty, chest pain, collapse, seizures or stroke symptoms: call 112/999. Severe new abdominal pain, major bleeding, worsening wounds or severe headache/visual change also need urgent assessment; tell the infusion nurse immediately about symptoms during a visit.

Full blood count, kidney and liver tests every three weeks for the first 12 months, then as clinically indicated. Check urine protein and blood pressure before each bevacizumab cycle; monitor blood pressure after treatment as advised. Review symptoms, wounds, medicines and tablet supply; extra tests may be needed.
Extra tests if symptoms, results or medicines change. Report illness rather than waiting for routine bloods.
Follow abnormal results and persistent symptoms; agree who will arrange any further tests.

rows.label: Blood pressure, urine and wounds
cells: Baseline blood pressure, urine protein, cardiac history/examination and wound/surgery assessment.
Urine protein and blood pressure before each bevacizumab cycle; review wounds and symptoms.
Bring readings if requested; report severe headache, visual changes, swelling, bleeding or wound problems.
Continue blood-pressure follow-up as advised and respect the postoperative/healing plan.

rows.label: Tablets and prescribed support
cells: Confirm dose, tablet strengths, medicines, support instructions and a reliable supply.
Check adherence, symptoms, intake and tablet supply at reviews.
Take tablets morning and evening; use only prescribed support. Contact the team if unable to take or keep down treatment.
Do not restart after a hold without the team’s instruction; agree the next prescription or safe return of unused tablets.

rows.label: Cancer response and duration
cells: This pathway requires a validated homologous recombination deficiency (HRD)-positive result, defined by a qualifying BRCA1/2 change and/or genomic instability, and response after first-line platinum chemotherapy with bevacizumab. HRD can be positive without a BRCA mutation. The team also checks histology, previous cycles, fitness and no previous PARP-inhibitor treatment.

The consultant sets symptom reviews, scans and any relevant CA-125 testing. Agree the total bevacizumab exposure and the separate two-year olaparib decision; safety blood/urine tests do not replace cancer assessment.
Report new pain, swelling, appetite change, breathing symptoms or other concerns promptly.

The medicines have separate treatment clocks. Bevacizumab is given for a maximum of 15 months in total, counting doses with the earlier chemotherapy. Olaparib has a two-year disease-status review: complete treatment at two years if no cancer is visible on scans; if disease remains, the consultant may consider further benefit from continuing. Either medicine may stop earlier for progression or unacceptable side effects. Finishing bevacizumab does not automatically finish olaparib.

rows.label: Pregnancy and family questions
cells: Discuss the validated test result, inherited implications and genetic counselling. Pregnancy testing and fertility discussion where relevant.
Continue agreed pregnancy prevention; repeat testing as advised.
Check new medicines and contraception with the team.

Follow the olaparib pregnancy-prevention advice, including two reliable complementary methods where relevant. Bevacizumab also requires effective contraception during treatment and for six months after its last dose; use the later applicable end date. Do not breastfeed during either treatment, for at least six months after the last bevacizumab dose, and for one month after the last olaparib dose—whichever date is later. Discuss fertility before treatment and tell the team immediately if pregnancy is possible.

longitudinal_schedule.note: Appointments are individual. Safety blood tests check treatment effects; scans and relevant cancer markers assess the disease. A reference calendar does not book an appointment or set the total course.

administration.cycle_and_sequence: Take the prescribed olaparib dose morning and evening every day, including between infusion visits. Bevacizumab is given into a vein on Day 1 of each 21-day interval after the checks. The two medicines have separate stop dates.
route_and_duration: Olaparib usually starts at 300 mg by mouth twice daily, with reviewed dose changes if needed. Bevacizumab is 15 mg/kg by intravenous infusion every 21 days. Follow the individual prescription and the separate duration decisions.
practical_workflow: Confirm the validated HRD result, response after first-line platinum-taxane chemotherapy with bevacizumab, and recovery. Check full blood count, kidney/liver profile, blood pressure, urine protein, medicines and pregnancy testing where relevant; review heart health, bleeding/clots, operations and wound healing.

Maintenance follows the first platinum-taxane and bevacizumab phase. The regimen specifies 6–9 platinum-taxane cycles and bevacizumab in the final chemotherapy cycles, with an interval-surgery allowance. Your team confirms the exact previous-treatment and recovery requirements before this combination starts.

Swallow the prescribed tablets whole with or without food, once in the morning and once in the evening. Do not chew, crush, dissolve or divide them. The usual starting dose is two 150 mg tablets each time (300 mg twice daily); your own dose may be lower. Check both tablet strength and tablet count after every prescription change. If you miss a dose, take the next normal dose at its usual time; do not double up. Do not substitute olaparib capsules for tablets. Avoid grapefruit juice and check other grapefruit or bitter-orange products with your pharmacist. Bevacizumab needs an intravenous cannula or suitable existing access. The team explains how long the visit and checks will take.

Agree a written anti-sickness plan with your team, including what is prescribed regularly, what is for rescue, and when to call if it is not working. NCCP classifies oral olaparib as moderate-to-high sickness risk, but a fixed intravenous chemotherapy anti-sickness cycle does not apply. Some people need prescribed support and others do not need routine prevention. A stomach-acid medicine may be considered for symptoms under local policy. Give the pharmacist a complete list of prescriptions, over-the-counter medicines, vitamins and herbal products. Some antibiotics, antifungals, seizure medicines and St John’s wort can change how much olaparib reaches your body. Even anti-sickness treatment needs checking: aprepitant can increase olaparib exposure. Do not start a borrowed support medicine, change the olaparib dose or restart a paused course yourself.
Ask why it is paused, which tests are next and when the team will contact you. Only the prescriber can confirm the restart dose. Do not take catch-up tablets.

Either medicine may stop earlier for progression or unacceptable side effects. Finishing bevacizumab does not automatically finish olaparib. The consultant sets symptom reviews, scans and any relevant CA-125 testing. Agree the total bevacizumab exposure and the separate two-year olaparib decision; safety blood/urine tests do not replace cancer assessment.

BRCA1 and BRCA2 help repair damaged DNA. A germline change is present in the body’s cells and may have implications for relatives. A tumour-only change does not by itself show that it is inherited. Ask which test you had, what the result means and whether genetic counselling is appropriate. A variant of uncertain significance is not automatically a treatment-qualifying result.
Confirm the next tests, review, tablet supply and verified daytime/out-of-hours contact numbers. Ask what to do if a result or prescription has not arrived.

The first bevacizumab infusion is usually 90 minutes. If tolerated, the second may take 60 minutes and later infusions 30 minutes. Checks, preparation and observation add to the visit; your unit confirms the actual schedule.

Tell the team before any planned operation, dental procedure or new wound. Bevacizumab affects healing; a passed surgery date does not mean a wound is healed. Continue prescribed blood-pressure treatment and bring any requested readings. Blood thinners and all new medicines need review because bleeding/clotting risks must be considered together.
observation_and_access: Oral tablets have no infusion duration. Swallow whole with or without food; do not crush, split, chew or dissolve. Capsules and tablets are not interchangeable; missed doses are not doubled.
Bevacizumab first infusion 90 minutes, second 60 if first tolerated, subsequent 30 if preceding infusion tolerated; no IV bolus. A 21-day infusion cycle does not create tablet rest days.

Check BP and urine before every bevacizumab cycle; measure BP after treatment. If warfarin is used, INR weekly until stable and then each cycle. Consider echocardiography with prior anthracycline or chest-wall radiotherapy.
